When selecting security questions, it is important to choose questions for which the answers are known only by the account holder. Avoid questions where the answers may be publicly known, easily guessable, or obtainable through brute force attacks. For instance, questions like "What is your mother's maiden name?" or "What is your date of birth?" might be known by family members or friends. Similarly, questions such as "What is your favorite color?" or "What is your favorite baseball team?" are easily guessable. Questions like "What is the first name of your favorite high school teacher?" could be vulnerable to brute force attacks if lists of popular first names are readily available.

It is also recommended to avoid questions with "public" answers that can be found through simple search engine queries or other readily available facts, such as "first school." Additionally, questions with a limited number of possible answers, like "What model was your first car?", can be exploited by attackers who can then prioritize guesses based on statistical likelihood. During penetration testing, it is important to determine if the application allows users to choose their own questions and to assess the number of allowed password reset attempts, as unlimited attempts can be exploited.

Examples include "What is your mother's maiden name?" or "What is your date of birth?". Some questions, like "What is the first name of your favorite high school teacher?", can even be subject to brute-force attacks if the answer is likely to be found on easily downloadable lists of popular names.
